arguments.subject: Re: Input needed by 2026-10-15 - AI tools and restricted information
arguments.body:
Note for Board meeting: AI tools and restricted information

1. Approved AI tools and use with restricted information
The Institute approves two AI tools: an enterprise AI assistant integrated with the document platform, and an enterprise chat service with data retention switched off. Consumer AI services, browser extensions and personal accounts are not approved for Institute work [1].

Public and internal information may be used with these approved tools. Restricted information must never be entered into any AI tool that sends data outside the Institute's environment, including the approved external chat service. Restricted information may only be processed by models hosted inside the Institute's private cloud, and only after a data protection review [2]. Staff remain accountable for checking AI output, which is treated as a draft, not a final product [3]. AI use cases involving restricted information are high-risk and require Digital Governance Board approval [5].

2. Retention of AI prompts and outputs
Prompts and outputs from approved AI tools are not records by default. They become records only when used in a decision or publication, at which point the final version is filed with the related record and takes on that record's retention period [6]. Retention generally runs from the end of the calendar year the record was closed, subject to legal holds [7]. No separate numeric retention period exists for raw, unused prompts/outputs.

Sources:
[1] Aurora Institute AI Use Policy, Approved tools
[2] Data Classification and Handling Guide, Using classified information with AI tools
[3] Aurora Institute AI Use Policy, Prohibited uses
[5] AI Use Case Intake Procedure, Risk levels and approval
[6] Aurora Institute Records Retention Schedule, AI prompts and outputs
[7] Aurora Institute Records Retention Schedule, How to read this schedule
